h2: Water Leak Repair Canggu – Tracing Hidden Leaks Before They Spread
intro: A pump running nonstop or a PDAM meter ticking while every tap stays closed almost always points to a hidden leak. Water leak repair in Canggu handles everything from a weeping fitting under a kitchen sink to a burst PPR pipe buried beneath a garden path. With so many villas built fast over former rice paddies, those quiet failures tend to announce themselves within the first few years of occupancy.

sections.h3: Why Canggu's Ground Conditions Make Leaks More Likely
sections.text: Berawa and Batu Bolong sit on soil that was once paddy field, which means the water table sits high year-round. That same groundwater pushes into poorly sealed septic lines and makes loose drain joints weep after heavy rain. Add rapid construction—villas going up where fields stood—and you get a lot of first-year surprises: untested fittings, undersized waste pipes, and shower trays that were never properly sloped. A small drip at a floor drain can quietly soak a subfloor before anyone notices the smell.

sections.h3: The Most Common Leak Scenarios We Handle Here
sections.text: Burst PVC or PPR runs behind bathroom walls top the list, followed by weeping shower cartridges and corroded floor-drain connections. Garden irrigation lines are another frequent call-out; a pinhole in a buried pipe floods a lawn overnight and shows up as a soggy patch near the pool overflow. In Pererenan, pump rooms take a real beating during the wet months, so a slow leak at a check valve can turn into a flooded utility space before anyone checks on it.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp for an Accurate Quote
sections.text: A short video of the affected area—under the sink, around the shower base, or the garden line in question—helps us pinpoint the problem fast. If you suspect a hidden leak, film your PDAM meter with every tap closed for about thirty seconds so we can gauge the flow rate. Add the street name and note whether the issue appeared after heavy rain or crept in slowly. We'll review the clips and reply on WhatsApp with what needs doing and a straightforward quote.

sections.h3: Preventing the Next Leak Before the Rainy Season Hits
sections.text: Walk your garden lines each dry month and look for soft spots or discoloured grass that hints at a buried drip. Check the pump room and pool overflow valve before October; a worn seal now saves a flooded floor later. Make sure floor drains slope away from the tile and that no one has stacked furniture over them. Because Canggu's water table rises sharply in the wet months, even a minor septic or drain backup can turn into a real mess if those small fixes are skipped.

faq.q: How do I know if my villa has a hidden leak?
faq.a: If the PDAM meter keeps turning while every tap is shut, or a sump pump cycles nonstop, there's almost certainly a slow leak somewhere in the walls, under a slab, or in a buried irrigation line.

faq.q: Do you cover all of Canggu?
faq.a: Yes—we work across Berawa, Batu Bolong, Echo Beach, Pererenan, Babakan, Padonan and the surrounding lanes. Send us a WhatsApp message with your street name and we'll confirm we can come out.

faq.q: Can a leaking shower cause structural damage to a villa?
faq.a: Absolutely—water wicking through tile grout or a cracked tray will soak subfloor joists within weeks. In fast-built villas where waterproofing was rushed, that dampness can reach electrical conduits and trigger corrosion well before visible mould appears.
